# RETRO: PR #13107 (team 3)

## What worked
- Neutral follow-up to Sol on "what does the issue's quoted error imply on base" resolved a severity disagreement without quoting Opus; Sol self-corrected with its own evidence.
- Opus's single-line mutants against the PR's own test gave crisp, publishable test-validity evidence.
- Short, command-only PR: no desktop resources needed; both reviewers finished quickly (Sol 6.9 + 3.3 min, Opus about 16 min).

## Process deviations (candid)
- **Incidental early read:** `pi_job.py wait/status` output includes `latest_text`, which exposed Sol's final headline to the coordinator before the Opus final existed. Not passed to Opus. Tooling suggestion: omit `latest_text` from `wait` output, or add a `--lifecycle-only` flag.
- **Opus report file:** the harness refuses subagent report Writes ("Subagents should return findings as text"). The report arrived via SubagentHandback. The coordinator extracted it from the transcript's SubagentHandback tool input into opus/report.md. The first extraction took the last assistant text (a short wrap-up) and is preserved as opus/report.attempt1-wrong-extract.md. Suggestion: the omarchy-reviewer prompt/brief should say "return the report as text", or review_team.py should provide a `save-handback` command.
- **Opus reviewer read-bound deviations (self-reported):** several parallel 50-line reads exceeded the 60-line aggregate; one `ls -la` resolved owner names. Content was read completely; no evidence affected.
- **Coordinator heredoc slip:** unquoted heredoc with backticks ran `latest_text` as a command while updating STATUS.md (harmless "command not found"); fixed the resulting blank in STATUS.md.
- The coordinator read Opus's full report from the hand-back message, which arrived after Sol's final was saved, so independence ordering held.

## Requirements snapshot note
- comment-requirements.md "Current model preference" still says new reviews use Opus 5.5 High; policy default is xhigh. The snapshot added an applicability note. Suggest updating the base file.

## Carry forward
- For curl-stubbed tests, check whether stubs honour `-o` early.
- The Cloudflare fallback still needs a live `up` run (64 MiB vs client max 50 MB); flagged only as a scope limit.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in stubbed, network-free runs, the fallback handles the failure reported in #13035. The issue quotes `Failed to fetch speed test endpoints`. The base script prints that only when the api.fast.com lookup yields no URLs without a jq error: a connection failure, an HTTP error under `curl -f`, or JSON without usable `targets`. On this head, each of those cases now probes Cloudflare and starts the unchanged traffic workers. When the probe also fails, the same readable error and exit status 1 remain. When fast.com answers normally, Cloudflare is never contacted. The request shapes (`__down?bytes=N` GET, `__up` POST) match the defaults of Cloudflare's own speed test client.

| api.fast.com lookup (stubbed) | Base | This head |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP error, connection failure, or JSON without targets | `Failed to fetch speed test endpoints`, exit 1 | Cloudflare probe, then workers (probe failure keeps the base error) |
| Valid targets | fast.com workers | fast.com workers, no Cloudflare request |
| 2xx with a non-JSON body (plain text, HTML) | jq parse error, exit 5 | unchanged: jq parse error, exit 5 |

The suggestions below concern the new test, plus two optional hardening points in the lookup that predate this PR.

### New test passes when uploads or rate output are broken

The two weak assertions in `test/shell.d/network-speedtest-test.sh`:

- **Upload assertion:** `grep -qE "POST .*__up|__up"` also matches the probe's own log line (`-X POST --data-binary probe .../__up`), so it passes without any upload worker call.
- **Rate assertion:** the first curl stub ignores `-o /dev/null`. It prints `x` for the download probe and 64 KiB of NUL bytes for each worker request, all into the script's stdout, so `[[ -n $down_out ]]` holds even when no rate line is printed. It also produces the `ignored null byte in input` warning on every run, and the `x` is glued to the first rate line (`x0.0`).

Deliberately broken copies of the head script, run against the PR's test (3 runs each):

```text
upload workers POST to __down instead of __up    -> test passes
upload fallback exits without any upload traffic -> test passes
rate lines never printed                         -> test passes
fallback removed (base behavior)                 -> test fails
download workers use a different byte count      -> test fails
```

**Impact:** test-only. The fallback itself works in the stubbed runs, but a regression in the upload direction or in rate output would not be caught.

**Suggested change:** assert on the worker call shape, for example `grep -q -- "--data-binary @- https://speed.cloudflare.com/__up"`. Make the stubs honour `-o` (or write their fake bodies to `/dev/null`), then assert a numeric line such as `grep -Eq '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9])?$' <<<"$down_out"`.

### Optional: lookup failures the fallback does not reach (pre-existing)

Both points exist on the base branch too. They limit which kinds of "unreachable" reach the new fallback:

- **Non-JSON success body.** The lookup assignment runs under `set -e` without `pipefail`, so jq's exit status decides. A 2xx response with a plain-text or HTML body makes jq exit 5 and ends the script before the fallback (reproduced with a stub; see the table above). Appending `|| true` to the assignment (optionally with `2>/dev/null` on jq) would send any unusable answer to the fallback.
- **No lookup timeout.** The api.fast.com request has no `--connect-timeout` or `--max-time`. curl 8.22.0 documents a 300 s default connect timeout. The speed test panel stops each phase after 5 s and treats that stop as expected (`shell/plugins/panels/speedtest/Panel.qml`). On a network that silently drops packets to api.fast.com, the panel would show neither the fallback result nor the readable error. A short timeout on the lookup, with the probe's `--max-time 5` reduced well below the panel's phase, would avoid that. This follows from source and curl documentation; no live timing was measured.

**Documentation note:** the worker comment "Round-robin across the returned URLs so we spread load across Netflix OCA nodes" no longer describes the single Cloudflare URL case.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned head `4bc1adc8`, read against base `quattro` at `28ceaae7`. Evidence came from source reading, the PR's test in a network-free sandbox (30 of 30 passes), stubbed lookup scenarios and single-line diagnostic mutations of the script. No request was made to api.fast.com or speed.cloudflare.com, so real endpoint behavior is untested. In particular, the upload workers post 64 MiB per request, while Cloudflare's own client uploads at most 50 MB per request, and no documented `__up` size limit was found. A live `up` run (the unticked item in the PR's test plan) would show whether that size is accepted. If Cloudflare rejects it, the workers stop and the script exits 0 with no output.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
